name: CLI-Anything
description: "CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native" -- CLI-Hub: https://clianything.cc/
one_liner: A toolkit and public library of command-line 'translators' that let AI agents operate ordinary software (like Blender, Obsidian, or Rekordbox) the same way a human would click through a GUI.
buyer: A software vendor's developer-relations team that wants their product to be usable by AI coding agents, but has no one internally who understands how to build that bridge.
business_use_cases: A small dev agency gets paid by niche software vendors to build and publish an 'agent-native CLI' for their product on the public hub, as a marketing and integration play.
An AI-agent integration shop uses it as the base layer to offer 'make any of your internal tools agent-usable' as a fixed-scope engagement for mid-size companies.
A contributor builds CLIs for popular creative or productivity apps and takes paid feature requests from companies wanting their software prioritized on the hub.

money_ideas.idea: Contract fee for building a vendor-specific agent-native CLI and publishing/maintaining it
Paid priority/sponsored listing or maintenance tier for vendors on CLI-Hub

steal_this: Pick one popular desktop app without an agent-native CLI yet, build a minimal wrapper with this framework over a weekend, publish it to the hub, and pitch the vendor directly.
